handoff: Review: a scalar means:/verdict: on an agent step is silently dropped (step-wording.ts:263; verdict: pass loads, verdict lost) — refuse it naming the step. AC1–AC13 traced, suite and typecheck green, golden decisions identical.

findings.title: A scalar `means:` or `verdict:` on an agent step is dropped without an error
findings.detail:
proseErrors skips a `means`/`verdict` value that is not a map (`if (!isObj(map)) continue; // the schema names the shape`). The schema never sees it: toModelStep drops both keys (line 293), and withProse treats a value that is not a map as {} (lines 302-303). Repro: parseWorkflowText on `steps: { a: { agent: do it, outcomes: { done: $done }, means: { done: built }, verdict: pass } }` loads to `outcomes.done = { to: $done, means: built }`. The verdict is lost, so criteria reporting changes without any error. `means: hello` on a step that routes only overridable outcomes also loads and is dropped. This breaks the slice goal (refuse malformed shapes, naming the step) and makes the comment at line 263 false.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: In proseErrors, refuse a `means`/`verdict` that is not a map, naming `/steps/<name>/<key>` (e.g. "`verdict:` is a map from outcome to verdict"), and add a test for each key.
